newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end lower on heavy profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end lower on heavy profit taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended sharply down on Tuesday on heavy profit-taking in secondaries with the focus on property firm PT Elang Realty, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index was off 9.30 points, or 1.42 percent, to close at 647.23 points after a low of 645.07 points. Decliners led advancers by 97 to 33 with 59 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 652.2 billion rupiah compared with 762 billion rupiah on Monday.
Brokers said the sharp fall of Elang Realty in the morning session before the exchange temporarily suspended trading in the issue had given a negative tone to overall market sentiment.
A broker with a local firm said the sharp fall in Elang's share price "triggered large profit-taking in other secondary stocks".

The price of Elang Realty, with interests in hotels, office buildings, housing and recreational facilities, dived 30.43 percent during the morning before the exchange suspended trading in its shares an hour before the lunch break.
The exchange lifted the trading ban in the early afternoon after saying it had found no irregularities.
Elang, the most active counter of the day with about 108 million shares changing hands, closed 300 rupiah lower at 1,425 after touching a high of 1,875 and a low of 1,125.
Brokers attributed Elang's earlier rise over the past few days to market talk of a possible rights issue.

Eddi J. Soebari, vice president of Bakrie Capital Indonesia, a holding company of the unlisted Bakrie group which holds 70 percent of Elang, said a rights issue would be discussed at an extraordinary general meeting of the property firm on May 9.
He said the Bakrie group also planned to change Elang's name to Bakrie Land. "There is no corporate action which is not known by the public," he told Reuters.
Brokers said weak regional markets coupled with the absence of positive domestic news had also dampened market sentiment.
Blue chip stocks such as cigarette maker Sampoerna, telecommunications firm Telkom and paper maker Indah Kiat were among targets for foreign profit takers, brokers said.
